paragraph: [The Open Budget Survey 2025 says the finance ministry published its citizens budget and in-year reports online on time](<https://internationalbudget.org/sites/default/files/country-surveys-pdfs/2025/open-budget-survey-angola-2025-en.pdf>). It asks the ministry to publish them in open formats, not only as PDFs. [The statistics office INE launched the Portal do Censo 2024 and the INE Angola app](<https://angop.ao/noticias/politica/ine-lanca-portal-do-censo-2024-e-aplicacao-movel/>), giving anyone online census indicators, tables and maps. [INE's own site publishes the definitive 2024 census results for download](<https://www.ine.gov.ao/publicacoes/detalhes/NDc0MTE%3D>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[In June 2025 INSBU's Accord de Licence Ouverte granted a free, worldwide, non-exclusive licence to use, copy, modify and distribute the platform's data](<https://www.insbu.bi/useragreement>). Derivative products are allowed, commercially or not, with attribution. [In November 2023 INSBU's acting director-general said all national statistics are published on a data portal anyone can consult](<https://lerenouveau.bi/insbu-la-publication-des-donnees-statistiques/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 names two or more public bodies publishing data. Operating would need two or more public bodies publishing data under an open licence, named or counted by a source from the past three years.

[In July 2025 a workshop prepared the migration of INStaD's Open Data portal of the national statistical system to its SDMX 2.0 version](<https://www.instad.bj/actualites/731-diffusion-des-donnees-statistiques-au-benin-l-instad-et-la-commission-de-l-uemoa-se-donnent-la-main-pour-la-migration-vers-la-nouvelle-version-du-portail-open-data>). [In 2025 ASIN ran the national portal data.gouv.bj](<https://numericite.eu/realisations/transformer-les-donnees-geospatiales-du-benin-en-levier-de-politique-publique/>). In the last twelve months, [in July 2026 the budget directorate's open-data API served budget classification data for 2008-2024](<https://backdata.budgetbenin.bj/public/api/agregats>). No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[In June 2026 CITADEL, at the Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo, listed 147 datasets on its national data portal](<https://data.citadel.bf/>), with twelve more in validation. [INSD, the statistics institute, licenses its data free of charge to anyone, worldwide](<https://www.insd.bf/fr/licence-data-insd>). The licence covers data on its website and open data portal, and allows copying, changes and commercial use with attribution. In the last twelve months, [CITADEL said its portal holds more than 145 datasets from more than 5 national agencies and official portals](<https://data.citadel.bf/>). That count of June 2026 meets the Mature test of four or more public bodies publishing. The portal has no public API.

[In August 2026 Statistics Botswana's own microdata portal showed the office moving toward publishing datasets for reuse](<https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/data-botswanas-new-diamond-taavi-erkkola-gdowf/>). [No dataset count was given, and the office was still exploring licensing, Creative Commons rather than non-commercial clauses](<https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/data-botswanas-new-diamond-taavi-erkkola-gdowf/>). In the last twelve months, this August 2026 report is the one source found, and no earlier position has been found to compare it with. No source found since October 2023 names two or more public bodies publishing data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[In May 2025 the country launched its National Summary Data Page](<https://ecomatin.net/le-fmi-annonce-un-nouveau-decaissement-de-334-milliards-fcfa-au-profit-de-la-centrafrique>), a portal of key macroeconomic and financial data. [The IMF says three public bodies publish on it: ICASEES, the regional central bank BEAC and the finance ministry](<https://www.imf.org/en/News/Articles/2025/05/19/pr-25153-central-african-republic-car-implements-enhanced-general-data-dissemination-system>). [ICASEES's education data page offers yearbook and key-indicator files for download, each under CC BY 4.0](<https://www.icasees.org/index.php/publications/tableau-de-bord/donnees-sectorielles/education-nationale>). In the last twelve months, [more than fifty indicators on ICASEES's platforms were updated in 2026](<https://www.icasees.org/index.php/actualites/398-icasees-la-troisieme-phase-dapurement-du-rgph-4-franchit-une-nouvelle-etape-vers-la-finalisation-des-resultats-du-recensement>). No source found since November 2024 names or counts a fourth body. Mature would need four or more public bodies publishing under an open licence.

[The 2024-2026 national open government action plan lists an open data portal among the government's initiatives since joining the OGP](<https://ogp.gouv.ci/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Plan-dAction-National-2024-2026-VF-signe.pdf>). Under commitment 6 it calls the portal running and to be enriched. [By June 2020, after training, the petroleum and renewable energy ministry had published around 50 new datasets on the data.gov.ci portal](<https://www.opengovpartnership.org/members/cote-divoire/commitments/CI0024/>). In the last twelve months, [in October 2026 the official open data portal of the Government Information and Communication Centre listed 211 datasets across five sectors](<https://data.gouv.ci/datasets>). No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[The INS launched its Open SDG platform on 17 September 2025](<https://leconomie.info/open-sdg-une-plateforme-pour-le-suivi-des-odd-au-cameroun/>), set up in 2024 with UNECA support. [In November 2025 an INS officer presented its Portail Open Data, Open SDG and ANADOC platforms](<https://ins-cameroun.cm/35%E1%B5%89-journee-africaine-de-la-statistique-le-littoral-mise-sur-linnovation-pour-une-donnee-au-service-du-developpement/>). In the last twelve months, [on 22 April 2026 the National Institute of Statistics unveiled platforms giving direct access to macroeconomic series and, through a national data archive, to survey microdata](<https://seasonmedia.net/cameroun-lins-simplifie-lacces-aux-donnees/>). No licence was stated. The INS is the one publisher on record. No source found since October 2023 names two or more public bodies publishing data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[The National Institute of Statistics (INS) launched data.gouv.cd on 23 February 2026](<https://data.rhinocerosoftware.co/posts/lancement-de-la-plateforme-des-donnees-ouvertes-de-la-rdc-1/>) as the national open data platform. [ITIE-RDC publishes extractive revenue, production, mining-rights and contract datasets in CSV, Excel and JSON as at November 2026](<https://www.itierdc.net/open-data/>), with a public API. [The Ministry of Mines publishes validated mining statistics files for 2017 to 2025](<https://www.mines.gouv.cd/public/statistique/pdf>), each stated to be open access. No licence is named for these. In the last twelve months, [the Banque Centrale du Congo opened a new site in August 2026 showing exchange rates, inflation and other indicators](<https://numerico.cd/2026/08/17/la-bcc-a-desormais-un-site-internet-2-0-new-look-plus-fonctionnel>), with no download stated. No one source found since October 2023 names two or more of these bodies publishing data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[The SYNA-MNV forest monitoring programme of the Ministry of Forest Economy publishes five datasets for download, the newest from 2024](<https://syna-mnv.cg/donnees-ouvertes>). [The programme publishes them under an open licence, asking only that reusers credit the source](<https://syna-mnv.cg/donnees-ouvertes>). In the last twelve months, [on 5 June 2026 the director general of the Institut national de la statistique said anyone can download data from its Open Data Portal](<https://www.vox.cg/le-congo-et-ses-partenaires-signent-un-accord-de-partenariat-pour-capitaliser-les-donnees-statistiques/>). That makes two public bodies offering data for download, and only the forest programme states an open licence. No source found since November 2024 names or counts four or more public bodies publishing data. Mature would need four or more public bodies publishing under an open licence.

[INSEED, the national statistics institute, runs a national microdata archive (NADA) whose catalogue held 15 datasets on 23 August 2026](<https://www.nada.inseed-comores.org/index.php/home>). [They include the 2025 agricultural census and the 2024 household survey; no open licence is stated](<https://www.nada.inseed-comores.org/index.php/home>). [On 29 August 2024 the UN country team and national partners presented the Open Data Comores portal in Moroni, giving free access to development data](<https://www.lagazettedescomores.com/soci%C3%A9t%C3%A9/acc%C3%A9l%C3%A9ration-des-odd-pr%C3%A9sentation-du-portail-des-donn%C3%A9es-.html>). In the last twelve months, [the household survey's cleaned data files and public anonymised version were dated April 2026](<https://www.nada.inseed-comores.org/index.php/catalog/15>). No source found since October 2023 names two or more public bodies publishing data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[The government launched the Portal da Transparência on 21 January 2026](<https://www.governo.cv/o-lancamento-do-portal-da-transparencia-representa-o-compromisso-do-governo-com-a-responsabilidade-publica-e-com-a-participacao-cidada-na-construcao-de-uma-sociedade-mais-justa-e-aberta/>). The minister said it shows in real time how public money is raised, planned and spent. [The OGP review says the finance ministry publishes budget execution and spending data on its website](<https://www.opengovpartnership.org/members/cabo-verde/commitments/CV0004/>). In the last twelve months, [the fisheries directorate has published fisheries data on its Fisheries Information System since January 2026](<https://fiti.global/cabo-verde-transforms-fisheries-transparency-with-new-fisheries-information-system-fis>), FiTI reports. The directorate, the Maritime and Port Institute and the National Institute of Statistics update it. No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[On 12 June 2025 Djibouti launched its National Summary Data Page under the IMF e-GDDS at the Central Bank](<https://www.lanation.dj/systeme-general-de-diffusion-des-donnees-ameliore-sgdd-a-djibouti-lance-sa-page-nationale-recapitulative-des-donnees/>). [Central Bank, INSTAD and Budget Ministry staff built it with the IMF and AfDB](<https://www.lanation.dj/systeme-general-de-diffusion-des-donnees-ameliore-sgdd-a-djibouti-lance-sa-page-nationale-recapitulative-des-donnees/>). [It is publicly accessible worldwide and hosted on the Djibouti Open Data Platform](<https://www.lanation.dj/systeme-general-de-diffusion-des-donnees-ameliore-sgdd-a-djibouti-lance-sa-page-nationale-recapitulative-des-donnees/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

No stage is set. No government data published for download has been found since October 2023, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. A dashboard with nothing to download, or a portal only planned, does not count. Preparing would need a public body publishing data online for anyone to download, on a portal or its own site, in the past three years.

[In June 2026 the Ministry of Agriculture's National Agri Data Hub listed 1,910 datasets in RDF and JSON-LD](<https://data.moa.gov.et/dataset/>). No data licence is stated. [The hub listed datasets from two public bodies, the Ministry of Agriculture and the Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research](<https://data.moa.gov.et/dataset/>). [The Ethiopian Statistics Service says in 2026 that it runs STATBANK, microdata repositories and web portals](<https://ess.gov.et/about-ess/departments/statistical-data-dissemination-and-access/>). In the last twelve months, the hub's June 2026 listing is the source found that names more than one public body publishing. No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[In February 2025 the download page of the Direction Générale de la Statistique offered files for anyone to download](<https://statgabon.ga/donnee_a_telecharcher/>). They include monthly consumer price indices, foreign trade bulletins, population projections and census results. The newest files date from April 2022, and the page gives no terms of reuse. In the last twelve months, [Gabon hosted a CEMAC and African Development Bank workshop on regional statistics platforms in September 2026](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-atelier-bad-cemac-14-recommandations-formulees/>). No source found since November 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[The Bank of Ghana launched a beta database portal on 5 February 2024 for extracting macroeconomic data](<https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Press-Release-Launch-of-Beta-Version-BOG-Database-Portal-05-02-2024.pdf>). It held 255 monthly and 86 quarterly series across five sectors, with no licence stated. [The World Bank said in December 2024 that 315 datasets had been uploaded to the Ghana Open Data portal since 2020](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099122324145517808/txt/BOSIB1971c4e0d0a219e2b1e9f369f20cb7.txt>). It added that the count had not grown for three years and the portal was down. In the last twelve months, [the National Information Technology Agency's Ghana Open Data Initiative catalogue was described in August 2026](<https://data.gov.gh/about>). No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[In 2017 the ITIE-Guinee steering committee's policy said five bodies publish revenue data on their own sites](<https://opendataitie-guinee.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/Politique-GMP-en-Matiere-de-donnees-Ouvertes.pdf>). They are the Ministry of Mines, CPDM, SOGUIPAMI, the Chambre des Mines and the central bank (BCRG). In the last twelve months, [from 20 to 25 July 2026 the INS held a workshop, with African Development Bank support, on migrating to its Open Data Platform (ODP) 2.0](<https://www.stat-guinee.org/index.php/actu/418-atelier-national-de-renforcement-des-capacites-sur-la-modelisation-sdmx-et-la-migration-vers-odp-2-0>). The platform is the system through which the INS disseminates official statistics, and participants recommended feeding it regularly. No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[In October 2026 the Gambia Bureau of Statistics offered GDP, CPI, PPI, trade and survey reports with microdata for download at gbosdata.org/downloads](<https://www.gbosdata.org/downloads>). [On 2 July 2026 its microdata catalogue held three survey studies: MICS 2000, DHS 2019-2020 and the Labour Force Survey 2018](<https://microdata.gbosdata.org/index.php/home>). The latest entries are dated June and July 2025. In the last twelve months, the bureau's catalogue of July 2026 is the latest dated source found. No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data or names two or more public bodies publishing it. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[The National Institute of Statistics says the page, hosted on the national Open Data Portal, was launched on 14 June 2024](<http://stat-guinebissau.com/Menu_principal/IV_RGPH/rgph1/COMUNICADO/Comunicado_Divulga%C3%A7%C3%A3o_Dados_e_GDDS_INE_FMI.pdf>). It is the National Summary Data Page, and it gives public access to key economic information. [In July 2024 the IMF said the page's data comes from the statistics institute, the finance ministry and the BCEAO](<https://www.imf.org/en/News/Articles/2024/07/08/pr24262-guinea-bissau-implements-imfs-enhanced-general-data-dissemination-system>). [In April 2015 the National Assembly's open data page published 4 open datasets in JSON via APIs](<https://www.parlamento.gw/transparencia/dados-abertos>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[In 2025 the civic technology group Pollicy said the Kenya Open Data Initiative portal gives free access to government data in machine-readable formats](<https://pollicy.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Policy-brief-13-Mar.pdf>). The portal it names is kenya.opendataforafrica.org. [President Kibaki launched the first national portal, opendata.go.ke, on 8 July 2011](<https://www.capitalfm.co.ke/news/2011/07/kenya-govt-data-released-on-internet/>). [The Open Government Partnership's record of Kenya's commitments says that portal later went offline](<https://www.opengovpartnership.org/members/kenya/commitments/KE0034/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[LISGIS, the statistics office, adopted CC BY 4.0 as its licence standard from 8 June 2026](<https://liberia.opendataforafrica.org/atrwrfc>). [Its notice grants anyone a free, worldwide licence to use and redistribute its data, including on its open data portal](<https://liberia.opendataforafrica.org/atrwrfc>). Commercial use is allowed with attribution. In the last twelve months, [the EITI said in July 2026 that LEITI's online data portal had made extractive data much more open](<https://eiti.org/documents/liberia-2026-validation-report>). It names two public sources of company production data: the LEITI Data Warehouse and the Ministry of Mines and Energy's online cadastre. No source found since November 2024 names four or more public bodies publishing data on a portal. Mature would need four or more public bodies publishing under an open licence.

[The General Information Authority launched the Open Government Data Platform on 27 November 2025](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2025/11/27/the-general-authority-for-information-launches-the-open-government-data-platform/>), with datasets, APIs and indicators. [Its terms let anyone use the datasets lawfully and republish them](<https://opendata.gia.gov.ly/terms.html>), crediting the platform and the dataset. [The authority reported 91 datasets on the platform in February 2026](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2026/02/11/includes-91-datasets-the-general-authority-for-information-launches-new-indicators-through-the-open-data-platform/>), with nine government bodies taking part across eight sectors. In the last twelve months, [the platform held 166 datasets by November 2026](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=370037&lang=ar>), the authority told the Libyan Permanent Economic Forum in Tripoli. [In September 2026 the communications authority listed its 2025 ICT workforce figures there as a downloadable spreadsheet](<https://opendata.gia.gov.ly/dashboard/dataset/432987>).

[In April 2025 the Bureau of Statistics Lesotho said all reports listed on its publications page can be downloaded](<https://www.bos.gov.ls/publications.htm>). [Excel tables are given for national accounts, CPI and GDP](<https://www.bos.gov.ls/publications.htm>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data or names two or more public bodies publishing it. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[The Agence de Développement du Digital manages the national open data portal, data.gov.ma, as its documentation page said in August 2026](<https://data.gov.ma/fr/documentations>). [In December 2024 the agency said connected APIs now publish the planning commission's employment, price and national accounts figures on the portal](<https://data.gov.ma/fr/actualites/publication-automatiques-des-donnees-des-apis-du-hcp>). [The Open Government Partnership's review counted over 500 datasets and over 70,000 downloads by the end of 2023](<https://www.opengovpartnership.org/members/morocco/commitments/MO0034/>). It says 37 institutions were updating datasets by then. In the last twelve months, [in December 2025 the national open data steering committee discussed a 2026 action plan](<https://data.gov.ma/fr/actualites/11eme-reunion-du-comite-de-pilotage-national-open-data>). No source found since November 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[In August 2026 the Assemblée nationale de Madagascar published five parliamentary datasets as JSON and CSV on its open data page and a read-only REST API](<https://parlement.mg/opendata/>). [The data is under Licence Ouverte v2.0 (compatible CC-BY), free to reuse including commercially with attribution](<https://parlement.mg/opendata/>). [In February 2025 the Ministry of Economy and Finance launched PortES, a socio-economic data portal with six components](<https://www.undp.org/fr/madagascar/actualites/portes-transparence-des-donnees-et-informations-socioeconomiques-madagascar>). In the last twelve months, the Assembly's August 2026 publication is the development found, and only the Assembly states an open licence. No source found since November 2024 names or counts four or more public bodies publishing data. Mature would need four or more public bodies publishing under an open licence.

[INSTAT's open data licence grants a free, worldwide, non-exclusive licence to use, copy, modify and distribute its datasets, tables, indicators and dashboards](<https://www.instat-mali.org/laravel-filemanager/files/shares/doc/conditions-utilisation-donnees-ouvertes_doc.pdf>). Derived products and commercial use are allowed with attribution. [In August 2026 INSTAT's data catalogue listed 107 studies, including the 2022 census (RGPH5) and agricultural surveys](<https://microdata.instat.ml/index.php/catalog/>). In the last twelve months, [in November 2026 FAO said INSTAT and CPS/SDR had published the 2023-24 agricultural survey results](<https://www.fao.org/in-action/agrisurvey/news/news-detail/mali-releases-2023-24-agricultural-data-under-the-50x2030-initiative/en>). No source found since October 2023 names two or more public bodies publishing data under the licence. Operating would need two or more public bodies publishing under an open licence.

[The Fundo de Estradas, a Mozambican public fund, runs the IPDP portal for data on road, bridge and other public infrastructure projects, and was validated as an OC4IDS publisher in 2026](<https://www.dadosinfra.co.mz/>). [The portal puts its data under a Creative Commons licence with attribution](<https://www.dadosinfra.co.mz/>). In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the fund published public infrastructure project data on that portal. No source found since October 2023 names two or more public bodies publishing data. Operating would need two or more public bodies publishing under an open licence.

[In November 2024 the EITI Board said Mauritania EITI makes extractive revenue, production and export data available on its Data Warehouse portal](<https://eiti.org/board-decision/2024-57>). [The data sets download in CSV](<https://eiti.org/board-decision/2024-57>). [Mauritania EITI is a government-backed multi-stakeholder body set up by Decree 2018-135](<https://eiti.org/board-decision/2024-57>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data or names two or more public bodies publishing it. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[On 22 October 2025 Statistics Mauritius and UNDP launched the MauStats data platform](<https://www.undp.org/mauritius-seychelles/news/undp-and-statistics-mauritius-launch-maustats-platform-world-statistics-day>), a hub built to SDMX standards. [The National Open Data Portal, set up under the May 2017 National Open Data Policy, releases government datasets as open data in CSV and XML](<https://dataprotection.govmu.org/Documents/NDS_final.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [on 3 September 2026 the Bank of Mauritius launched BOMStats, its statistical data platform](<https://www.bom.mu/media/media-releases/bank-mauritius-expands-access-official-statistics-rollout-bomstats-platform>). It offers an API and SDMX-format data sharing. No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[On 3 September 2025 the OGP Malawi Secretariat announced the launch of Malawi's new Open Data Portal](<https://ogp.gov.mw/events/malawi-launches-new-open-data-portal>). [It gives citizens budget, development project and public service delivery data through dashboards and downloadable datasets](<https://ogp.gov.mw/events/malawi-launches-new-open-data-portal>). It is part of the Third OGP National Action Plan. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data or names two or more public bodies publishing it. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[In August 2026 the Namibia Statistics Agency's microdata catalogue listed 16 studies](<https://nsa.org.na/data-portals/>). Most were marked open access. [They include the 2023 census public-use microdata sample, last modified on 21 July 2026](<https://nsa.org.na/data-portals/>). In the last twelve months, on 18 November 2026, [the agency launched a public online portal for the Sustainable Development Goals](<https://neweralive.na/ngurare-demands-data-accountability-as-country-launches-sdg-portal/>). No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data or names two or more public bodies publishing it. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.

[Under a licence dated 30 October 2024, Niger's Institut National de la Statistique lets anyone use, modify and distribute its data](<https://www.stat-niger.org/?page_id=4877>). [The worldwide, free, non-exclusive licence covers commercial and non-commercial use, with attribution](<https://www.stat-niger.org/?page_id=4877>). [In May 2025 the World Bank said the national Open Data Portal, with some of its data, is accessible on the statistics office's website](<https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/opendata/improving-access-to-quality-data-in-fragility-and-conflict-conte>). [On 18 September 2025 the national nutrition information platform PNIN launched its renovated portal, with a download space](<https://pnin-niger.org/web/?p=3641>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 names two or more public bodies publishing data. Operating would need two or more public bodies publishing under an open licence.

[In October 2026 Anambra State Government launched a redesigned website whose Open Government section gives access to budgets, audit reports, procurement plans, contract awards and open data](<https://techtrends.africa/anambra-launches-digital-gateway-to-unify-government-services-open-data-and-citizen-engagement/>). No dataset count or licence is given. [The 2018 national open data policy names Data.gov.ng as the national catalogue of open data](<https://nipc.gov.ng/assets/resources/nigeria-open-data-policy/nigeria-open-data-policy.pdf>), and requires agencies to link their datasets to it. In the last twelve months, the October 2026 launch is the one development found. Anambra is the one publisher on record, at the level of one state. No open licence for the data has been found since November 2023. Establishing would need the data published under an open licence, or terms that let anyone reuse it.
